name: Shrimply Well-Seasoned Pasta
sub: Creamy garlic-butter-style shrimp scampi with protein pasta, broccoli, and red cabbage · 4 generous servings
text:
YIELD
4 generous servings

INGREDIENTS
Shrimp, Pasta & Vegetables
1 lb (16 oz) raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
4 oz dry Al Dente Protein Pasta
12 oz red cabbage, thinly sliced
8 oz broccoli, cut into bite-size pieces
1¾ tsp avocado oil
2 Tbsp water, for steaming broccoli

Homemade Scampi Seasoning
1 Tbsp garlic powder
1 tsp onion powder
1 tsp dried parsley
1 tsp dried lemon zest
½ tsp fine salt
½ tsp sugar
½ tsp citric acid (optional; see Notes)
¼ tsp black pepper
¼ tsp red pepper flakes
¼ tsp dried basil or dried oregano

Creamy Scampi Sauce
1 cup Kroger Plain Nonfat Greek Yogurt
1 Tbsp lemon juice
¼–¾ cup reserved pasta water, as needed

Well-Seasoned Spice Boost
1 tsp garlic powder
½ tsp onion powder
½ tsp smoked paprika
½ tsp black pepper
¼ tsp ground thyme
⅛ tsp additional crushed red pepper (optional, for extra heat)

DIRECTIONS
1. Mix the seasoning. Stir together all Homemade Scampi Seasoning ingredients in a small bowl. Use the whole blend for this recipe. Keep the separate Spice Boost quantities additional to this blend.
2. Cook the pasta. Cook according to package directions until just al dente. Before draining, reserve ¾ cup pasta water. Drain without rinsing.
3. Steam the broccoli. Place broccoli and 2 Tbsp water in a large skillet over medium heat. Cover and steam for 3–4 minutes, until bright green and beginning to soften. Uncover, let remaining water evaporate, then transfer broccoli to a bowl.
4. Brown the cabbage. Add avocado oil to the skillet. Add cabbage and cook over medium-high heat for 5–7 minutes, tossing occasionally, until softened with a few browned edges. If the skillet becomes dry, add 1 Tbsp water at a time to prevent scorching.
5. Cook the shrimp. Add shrimp, the entire Homemade Scampi Seasoning blend, and all Spice Boost ingredients to the cabbage. Toss well. Cook for approximately 3–5 minutes, stirring frequently, until shrimp are opaque throughout. Shrimp size affects cooking time.
6. Combine. Reduce heat to low. Return broccoli to the skillet and add drained pasta. Toss thoroughly, then remove the skillet from the heat.
7. Make the sauce. Whisk yogurt, ¼ cup warm—not boiling—reserved pasta water, and 1 Tbsp lemon juice in a bowl until smooth.
8. Finish off the heat. Fold the yogurt mixture into the shrimp, pasta, and vegetables. Add remaining reserved pasta water 1–2 Tbsp at a time until the sauce coats everything. Serve immediately. Do not boil after adding yogurt.

NOTES
Use the full cup of Greek yogurt for enough sauce to coat the pasta and vegetables.
No commercial seasoning packet is needed; the homemade blend replaces it entirely.
Lemon pepper option: replace 1 tsp dried lemon zest with ½ tsp lemon pepper. If the lemon pepper contains salt, reduce fine salt in the blend to ¼ tsp.
Citric acid option: if omitting the ½ tsp citric acid, use 1½ Tbsp lemon juice in the sauce instead of 1 Tbsp.
No lemon zest or lemon pepper: omit the zest and increase lemon juice to 1½ Tbsp total. If also omitting citric acid, use 2 Tbsp lemon juice total. Keep the listed ½ tsp fine salt. These substitutions slightly change the estimated nutrition.
The base blend already contains ¼ tsp red pepper flakes. Include the additional ⅛ tsp only for extra heat.
For a smokier finish, replace ¼ tsp of the blend’s fine salt with ¼ tsp fine smoked salt; do not add it on top of the listed salt. If using salted lemon pepper, replace the remaining ¼ tsp fine salt with ¼ tsp fine smoked salt.
The garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper in the Spice Boost are intentionally additional to the homemade seasoning blend.

MACROS
Estimated per serving (¼ recipe): 291 kcal · 33.5 g protein · 3.8 g fat · 33.4 g total carbohydrate · 8.2 g fiber · 25.2 g net carbs · 940 mg sodium.
Estimated whole recipe: 1165 kcal · 133.9 g protein · 15.1 g fat · 133.7 g total carbohydrate · 32.7 g fiber · 100.9 g net carbs · 3,760 mg sodium.
Basis: Kroger raw shrimp label (80 kcal, 15 g protein, 550 mg sodium per 4 oz); Kroger yogurt label (1 cup = 255 g); Al Dente Protein Egg Fettuccine label (180 kcal, 17 g protein, 32 g carbs, 8 g fiber, 1.5 g fat, 55 mg sodium per 2 oz dry); standard reference estimates for vegetables, oil, herbs, and spices. Includes all Spice Boost quantities, dried lemon zest, basil, ½ tsp fine salt, and unsalted pasta cooking water. Excludes optional extra red pepper and citric acid. Other pasta or shrimp labels change the totals. Salted cooking water adds unquantified sodium.
